speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) strives to enable all Singaporeans to realise their potential.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have been engaging our stakeholders as part of the Forward Singapore exercise.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will strengthen our partnerships with families, communities, and industry to refresh our system of meritocracy, so that all can thrive and contribute to Singapore in their own ways.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: MOE is committed to providing a quality education and a strong foundation for every child.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In a complex and fast-changing world, our students will require diverse skillsets to stay resilient, and diverse perspectives to connect and collaborate with others in Singapore and elsewhere.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: MOE will thus continue to encourage holistic development and cultivate 21st Century Competencies.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: To meet the wider and more complex needs of our students, we will support our educators by giving them opportunities to broaden their perspectives and skillsets.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will also partner families and the community to provide holistic support for our children’s socio-emotional development.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have moved away from a one-size-fits-all approach to education, and from using a single metric to evaluate the diverse dimensions of our students’ abilities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will also step up our efforts to provide opportunities for learners of different backgrounds to interact, empathise with, and support one another.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: At the same time, to adapt to a changing global landscape, we will need to break new ground.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: First, amidst economic transformation and labour market disruptions, we must evolve our practices to create new value and stay ahead of the competition.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: At the same time, our people will need to make full use of these opportunities by developing a growth mindset and passion for lifelong learning.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will continue to strengthen the educational experience for students with SEN in mainstream and Special Education (SPED) schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This will improve the quality of SPED and better enable our students to lead independent and meaningful lives.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Third, we will leverage technology to better customise teaching and learning for students of different abilities.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will continue to invest in education technologies to bring out the best in each child.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: All of us have a part to play in shaping and strengthening our social compact.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Those who have done well in life should pay it forward, and support those who have less.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Success must be defined not just by one’s achievements, but also by how we contribute to the common good.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: By moving beyond the pursuit of paper qualifications and embracing a broader definition of success, our education system can bring out the best in every child and strengthen our resilience as a nation through our diversity of strengths.
